title: Release Runner
description: Synthetic flag evaluations and metric events that drive real guarded release decisions — demo a healthy rollout or force an auto-rollback on demand.
longDescription: A local Node.js app that generates synthetic flag evaluations and metric events (errors, latency, conversions) against a LaunchDarkly flag — driving guarded release decisions without real app traffic. Error, latency, and conversion rates are configurable, so you can demo a healthy progressive rollout or force a failing one that auto-rolls back in front of the customer.

A live WebSocket dashboard shows the control/treatment split in real time. Simulated users evaluate the flag through the LD Node Server SDK — the exact same variationDetail() call a real application makes — so the guarded release monitors genuine SDK traffic.

Run it locally: npm install && npm start. You'll need a server-side SDK key, a REST API token, and a flag with a guarded release configured on it. Expect metrics to take ~5–15 minutes to surface in LaunchDarkly. Note: the guarded release makes real advance/rollback decisions, so point it at a test environment.

flags.name: Guarded Release Target
flags.description: The flag Release Runner evaluates and sends metrics against. Configure a guarded release on it in LaunchDarkly, then point the runner at this key.
